sections.text: Przedmiot zamówienia obejmuje dostawę i wdrożenie systemu sterowania ruchem z priorytetem dla tramwajów na dwóch skrzyżowaniach ulicy Marymoncka – wjazd do KS Hutnik oraz Marymoncka – TMP (węzeł tramwajowy) na terenie Warszawy. Przedmiot zamówienia, w tym zakres zamówienia podstawowego oraz zamówienia z prawa opcji, określono szczegółowo w rozdziale II SWZ.

sections.label: 참가·선정 기준
sections.text: Doświadczenie Wykonawcy - o udzielenie zamówienia mogą ubiegać się Wykonawcy, którzy spełniają warunek udziału w postępowaniu dotyczący zdolności technicznej lub zawodowej, tj. Wykonawcy, którzy należycie wykonali w okresie ostatnich 5 lat (licząc wstecz od dnia, w którym upływa termin składania ofert), a jeżeli okres prowadzenia działalności jest krótszy – w tym okresie, co najmniej: 1) dwa projekty wykonawcze (wraz z ich uzgodnieniem) branży elektrycznej dla przebudowy lub budowy sygnalizacji świetlnej, uwzgledniające dowolną formę detekcji tramwajów dla skrzyżowania z ruchem tramwajowym w granicach administracyjnych miasta o liczbie ludności min. 250 000 mieszkańców; 2) dostawę i wdrożenie systemu sterowania ruchem z priorytetem dla tramwajów w sygnalizacji świetlnej wraz z oprogramowaniem na co najmniej 5 skrzyżowaniach (5 skrzyżowań w ramach jednej umowy lub sumarycznie 5 skrzyżowań w ramach kilku umów/zamówień) z zastosowaniem algorytmów sterowania akomodacyjnego wykorzystujących detekcję tramwajów. Uwaga: 1) przez sygnalizację świetlną należy rozumieć ogół rozwiązań w postaci systemów sterowania ruchem drogowym na skrzyżowaniach dróg publicznych, w tym na przejściach dla pieszych i przejazdach dla rowerów; sygnalizacją świetlną w myśl powyższej definicji nie jest sygnalizacja kolejowa na przejazdach kolejowych oraz w tunelach metra; 2) przez liczbę ludności należy rozumieć stan zaludnienia ogółem w danym mieście według oficjalnych danych Banku Danych Lokalnych Głównego Urzędu Statystycznego – podgrupa „ludność w gminach bez miast na prawach powiatu i w miastach na prawach powiatu wg płci” (a w przypadku doświadczenia zdobytego poza granicami Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej – według oficjalnych danych statystycznych właściwych dla danego kraju), przypadający dla okresu doświadczenia, na które powołuje się Wykonawca; ww. stan zaludnienia to stan na co najmniej jeden dowolny dzień w okresie opracowania danego projektu. W celu wstępnego potwierdzenia, że Wykonawca /każdy z Wykonawców wspólnie ubiegających się o zamówienie, spełnia warunki udziału w postępowaniu, należy złożyć wraz z ofertą aktualne na dzień składania ofert oświadczenie w formie Jednolitego Europejskiego Dokumentu Zamówienia (JEDZ) - można ograniczyć się do wypełnienia w części IV JEDZ jedynie sekcji α (alfa) i w takim przypadku nie trzeba wypełniać żadnej z pozostałych sekcji w części IV JEDZ. Wykonawca, który polega na zdolnościach lub sytuacji podmiotów udostępniających zasoby, musi złożyć wraz z ofertą zobowiązanie podmiotu udostępniającego zasoby do oddania mu do dyspozycji niezbędnych zasobów na potrzeby realizacji zamówienia lub inny podmiotowy środek dowodowy potwierdzający, że Wykonawca realizując zamówienie, będzie dysponował niezbędnymi zasobami tych podmiotów. Zamawiający przed wyborem najkorzystniejszej oferty wezwie Wykonawcę, którego oferta została najwyżej oceniona, do złożenia w wyznaczonym terminie, nie krótszym niż 10 dni, wykazu dostaw/usług wykonanych w okresie ostatnich 5 lat (licząc wstecz od dnia, w którym upływa termin składania ofert), a jeżeli okres prowadzenia działalności jest krótszy - w tym okresie, wraz z podaniem ich przedmiotu, dat wykonania i podmiotów, na rzecz których dostawy/usługi zostały wykonane lub są wykonywane, oraz załączeniem dowodów określających czy te dostawy/usługi zostały wykonane lub są wykonywane należycie, przy czym dowodami, o których mowa, są referencje bądź inne dokumenty sporządzone przez podmiot, na rzecz którego dostawy/usługi zostały wykonane, a jeżeli Wykonawca z przyczyn niezależnych od niego nie jest w stanie uzyskać tych dokumentów – oświadczenie Wykonawcy; jeżeli Wykonawca powołuje się na doświadczenie w realizacji dostaw/usług, wykonywanych wspólnie z innymi Wykonawcami, wykaz, o którym mowa powyżej, dotyczy dostaw/usług, w których wykonaniu Wykonawca ten bezpośrednio uczestniczył. | Wykształcenie personelu - o udzielenie zamówienia mogą ubiegać się Wykonawcy, którzy wykażą, że dysponują następującymi osobami zdolnymi do wykonania zamówienia, które zostaną skierowane do jego realizacji: 1) w zakresie projektowania instalacji sygnalizacji świetlnej – co najmniej 1 osobą: a) posiadającą uprawnienia budowlane bez ograniczeń do projektowania w specjalności instalacyjnej w zakresie sieci, instalacji i urządzeń elektrycznych i elektroenergetycznych, oraz b) posiadającą doświadczenie nabyte w okresie ostatnich 5 lat (licząc wstecz od dnia, w którym upływa termin składania ofert) przy opracowaniu (samodzielnie lub jako członek zespołu projektowego) co najmniej 2 projektów wykonawczych branży elektrycznej dla przebudowy lub budowy sygnalizacji świetlnej uwzgledniających dowolną formę detekcji dla skrzyżowania z ruchem tramwajowym; 2) w zakresie programowania sterowników sygnalizacji świetlnej – co najmniej 2 osobami, z których każda w okresie ostatnich 5 lat (licząc wstecz od dnia, w którym upływa termin składania ofert) przeprowadziła implementacje algorytmów sterowania akomodacyjnego z priorytetem dla tramwajów dla co najmniej 3 sterowników sygnalizacji świetlnej; 3) w zakresie wykonania instalacji sygnalizacji świetlnej – co najmniej 1 osobą: a) posiadającą uprawnienia budowlane bez ograniczeń do kierowania robotami budowlanymi w specjalności instalacyjnej w zakresie sieci, instalacji i urządzeń elektrycznych i elektroenergetycznych, oraz b) posiadającą doświadczenie nabyte w okresie ostatnich 5 lat (licząc wstecz od dnia, w którym upływa termin składania ofert) pełniąc funkcję kierownika robót elektrycznych przy zrealizowaniu co najmniej 2 robót budowlanych (od rozpoczęcia robót do ich zakończenia potwierdzonego protokołem odbioru lub równoważnym dokumentem), których przedmiotem każdej była budowa, przebudowa lub remont instalacji sygnalizacji świetlnej, 4) w zakresie projektowania czasowej organizacji ruchu z sygnalizacją świetlną – co najmniej 1 osobą, która w okresie ostatnich 5 lat (licząc wstecz od dnia, w którym upływa termin składania ofert) opracowała (samodzielnie lub jako członek zespołu projektowego) co najmniej 2 projekty czasowej organizacji ruchu dla robót wykonywanych przy czynnym ruchu tramwajowym obejmujące skrzyżowania z sygnalizacją świetlną w granicach administracyjnych miasta o liczbie ludności min. 1 mln, dla których uzyskano zatwierdzenia organu zarządzającego ruchem. Zamawiający dopuszcza wykazanie tej samej osoby do pełnienia więcej niż jednej funkcji; za zrealizowaną robotę budowlaną Zamawiający uzna doprowadzenie do wystawienia Świadectwa Przejęcia (dla kontraktów realizowanych zgodnie z warunkami FIDIC), Protokołu odbioru całości robót lub równoważnego dokumentu (w przypadku zamówień, w których nie wystawia się Świadectwa Przejęcia); w związku z powyższym za doświadczenie nabyte „przy zrealizowaniu” roboty budowlanej Zamawiający uzna pełnienie funkcji w ciągłym okresie zrealizowanej roboty budowlanej, bezpośrednio poprzedzającym wystawienie Świadectwa Przejęcia (dla kontraktów realizowanych zgodnie z warunkami FIDIC), Protokołu odbioru całości robót lub równoważnego dokumentu (w przypadku zamówień, w których nie wystawia się Świadectwa Przejęcia) wraz z doprowadzeniem do ich wystawienia; przez sygnalizację świetlną należy rozumieć ogół rozwiązań w postaci systemów sterowania ruchem drogowym na skrzyżowaniach dróg publicznych, w tym na przejściach dla pieszych i przejazdach dla rowerów; sygnalizacją świetlną w myśl powyższej definicji nie jest sygnalizacja kolejowa na przejazdach kolejowych oraz w tunelach metra; przez liczbę ludności należy rozumieć stan zaludnienia ogółem w danym mieście według oficjalnych danych Banku Danych Lokalnych Głównego Urzędu Statystycznego – podgrupa „ludność w gminach bez miast na prawach powiatu i w miastach na prawach powiatu wg płci” (a w przypadku doświadczenia zdobytego poza granicami Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej – według oficjalnych danych statystycznych właściwych dla danego kraju), przypadający dla okresu doświadczenia, na które powołuje się Wykonawca; ww. stan zaludnienia to stan na co najmniej jeden dowolny dzień w okresie opracowania danego projektu. W celu wstępnego potwierdzenia, że Wykonawca/każdy z Wykonawców wspólnie ubiegających się o zamówienie/podmiot udostępniający zasoby spełnia warunki udziału w postępowaniu, należy złożyć wraz z ofertą aktualne na dzień składania ofert oświadczenie w formie Jednolitego Europejskiego Dokumentu Zamówienia (JEDZ) - można ograniczyć się do wypełnienia w części IV JEDZ jedynie sekcji α (alfa) i w takim przypadku nie trzeba wypełniać żadnej z pozostałych sekcji w części IV JEDZ. Wykonawca, który polega na zdolnościach podmiotów udostępniających zasoby, musi złożyć wraz z ofertą zobowiązanie podmiotu udostępniającego zasoby do oddania mu do dyspozycji niezbędnych zasobów na potrzeby realizacji zamówienia lub inny podmiotowy środek dowodowy potwierdzający, że Wykonawca realizując zamówienie, będzie dysponował niezbędnymi zasobami tych podmiotów. Zamawiający przed wyborem najkorzystniejszej oferty wezwie Wykonawcę, którego oferta została najwyżej oceniona, do złożenia w wyznaczonym terminie, nie krótszym niż 10 dni wykazu osób, skierowanych przez Wykonawcę do realizacji zamówienia publicznego, w szczególności odpowiedzialnych za świadczenie usług lub kierowanie robotami budowlanymi, wraz z informacjami na temat ich uprawnień i doświadczenia niezbędnych do wykonania zamówienia publicznego, a także zakresu wykonywanych przez nie czynności oraz informacją o podstawie do dysponowania tymi osobami.

notices.title: Finland – Software package and information systems – Titania -työvuorosuunnittelukokonaisuuden päivitys

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text: Pohteella on voimassa oleva sopimus CGI Suomi Oy:n kanssa työvuorosuunnitteluun liittyvien Titania-järjestelmien toimittamisesta ja ylläpitopalveluista. Hyvinvointialuetta edeltäneiltä organisaatioilta (sairaanhoitopiirin, peruspalvelukuntayhtymät ja kunnat) on voimaanpanolain (616/2021) perusteella siirretty Titania-sopimukset Pohteelle ja ne on yhdistetty muutossopimuksella yhdeksi sopimukseksi, arvoltaan noin 3,6 miljoonaa euroa. Hyvinvointialueen toiminnan alkaessa sopimusta on laajennettu kattamaan loput työajanseurannan piiriin kuuluvat työntekijät. Laajennuksesta on julkaistu sopimusmuutosilmoitus. Nykyinen Pohteen käytössä oleva järjestelmä toimii on-premise- ja SaaS-palvelun yhdistelmänä eli osittain Pohteen palvelinympäristössä ja osittain toimittajan pilvipalvelussa (SaaS). Titania-järjestelmä on tarkoitus päivittää versioon 2.0. joka tuotetaan kokonaisuutena toimittajan pilvestä. Päivitykseen ei sisälly lisäominaisuuksia tai moduuleja. Hankintalain 136 §:n 2 mom. 2 kohta: Hankintasopimukseen voidaan tehdä muutos ilman uutta hankintamenettelyä, jos alkuperäisen sopimuskumppanin on tarpeen suorittaa lisätöitä tai -palveluja taikka ylimääräisiä tavarantoimituksia, jotka eivät sisältyneet alkuperäiseen sopimukseen, ja jos sopimuskumppanin vaihtaminen ei ole mahdollista taloudellisista tai teknisistä syistä ja aiheuttaisi merkittävää haittaa tai kustannusten merkittävää päällekkäisyyttä hankintayksikölle. Muutoksen arvo ei saa olla enemmän kuin 50 prosenttia alkuperäisen sopimuksen arvosta. Jos muutoksia tehdään peräkkäin useampia, arvioidaan jokaista muutosta itsenäisenä. Olemassa olevaan järjestelmään versiopäivitystä ei teknisistä syistä voida hankkia muilta toimittajilta kuin olemassa olevan järjestelmän sopimustoimittajalta. Sopimusmuutoksen arvo on alkuperäisen yhdistetyn sopimuksen arvon perusteella laskettuna noin 33 %. Muutos on siis alle lain salliman enimmäismäärän 50 %.

sections.text: Beschaffung und Einführung einer Mobile-Device-Management-Lösung (On-Premise)

sections.label: 세부 사업 내용
sections.text: Gegenstand des Auftrags sind Leistungen zur Beschaffung und Einführung einer Mobile-Device-Management-Lösung (On-Premise). Die Lösung muss den Betrieb von aktuell rund 5.000 mobilen Endgeräten (Smartphones, Tablets) zentral verwalten, absichern und kontrollieren. Es werden zu 95% iOS Geräte einsetzt und zu 5% Android. Im Einzelnen auftragsgegenständlich sind die Lieferung, Lizenzierung und Installation der Software in der IT-Infrastruktur des Auftraggebers (On-Premise), Einrichtung und Konfiguration gemäß den betrieblichen Anforderungen des Auftraggebers, Migration der bestehenden Geräte-, Profil- und Richtlinienbestände aus der aktuellen MDM-Umgebung, Schulung der administrierenden Mitarbeitenden sowie Support, Wartung und Pflege einschließlich Sicherheitsupdates über die gesamte Vertragslaufzeit.

sections.label: 참가·선정 기준
sections.text: Handelsregisterauszug: Nachweis der Eintragung im Handelsregister des Staates, in dem der Bieter niedergelassen ist, der nicht älter als drei Monate zum Zeitpunkt des Ablaufs der Angebotsfrist sein darf. Ist ein Bieter nach dem Recht des Staates, in dem er niedergelassen ist, nicht zur Eintragung in ein Berufs- oder Handelsregister verpflichtet, hat er darüber und über die Gründe (z.B. die Rechtsform) eine entsprechende Eigenerklärung abzugeben. Alternativer Nachweis: Sofern der Bieter nicht im Handelsregister verzeichnet ist, genügt der Nachweis der erlaubten Berufsausübung auf andere Weise (z.B. Eintragung in ein Partnerschafts- oder Vereinsregister, Mitgliedschaft in einer wirtschaftsständischen Vereinigung). | Anzugeben sind die Gesamtjahresumsätze (netto) bezogen auf die letzten drei abgeschlossenen Geschäftsjahre. | Spezifische Jahresumsätze (netto) für Leistungen im Tätigkeitsbereich des Auftrags (Liefer- und Dienstleistungen im Zusammenhang mit Mobile-Device-Management-Lösungen) bezogen auf die letzten drei abgeschlossenen Geschäftsjahre. Mindestanforderung: Der spezifische Umsatz (netto) für Leistungen im Tätigkeitsbereich des Auftrags (Liefer- und Dienstleistungen im Zusammen-hang mit Mobile-Device-Management-Lösungen) muss im Durschnitt der letzten drei abgeschlossenen Geschäftsjahre mindestens EUR 2.500.000,00 betragen haben. | Einzureichen ist der Nachweis einer Betriebshaftpflichtversicherung für Personen-, Sach- und Vermögensschäden für Tätigkeiten, die Gegenstand dieses Auftrags sind. notices.title: Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for New CADSS/MAJAID Facility

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) – TRS18081_73944 – New CADSS/MAJAID Facility, Trenton, Ontario

Defence Construction Canada (DCC) invites general contractors to express their interest in providing all labour, materials, and equipment necessary to build a new warehouse and operations facility to support the Combat Aerial Delivery Support Section/Major Air Disaster (CADSS/MAJAID) Unit.

This Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) is the first step of a two-step solicitation process, the second step being the Tender Phase.  Only general contractors that have expressed their interest through the Electronic Bidding System prior to the closing date and time of this RFEOI will be invited to submit a proposal at the second stage. Only submissions received in accordance with the requirements of the Electronic Bidding System will be considered.
Only the general contractors who will have responded to this RFEOI will be invited to submit a bid during the Tender Phase.

DCC reserves the right to terminate this solicitation at the end of the RFEOI.

As part of Canada’s commitment to maximize the participation of Indigenous Businesses, bidders are advised that this solicitation includes an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP). The Contractor will have to include Indigenous businesses (or eligible joint ventures) as subcontractors or suppliers to this project. Further details will be provided in the Tender phase.
This solicitation is being conducted in accordance with the requirements set out in the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA).

1. Project background
The CADSS/MAJAID Facility project at 8 Wing CFB Trenton consists of the construction of a new 1,554 m² warehouse and operations facility to support the Combat Aerial Delivery Support Section/Major Air Disaster (CADSS/MAJAID) Unit. The work comprises general contracting services and the supply and installation of all labour and materials required to construct the facility, including associated building systems and site infrastructure. The facility will provide space for parachute inspection, drying, preparation, and packing activities, while also accommodating administrative functions, operational storage requirements, and material handling activities.

The proposed facility includes a dedicated carpentry shop, warehouse storage areas, administrative office space, and specialized infrastructure to support operational equipment and warehouse activities involving forklifts and other machinery. Key features include storage and racking systems, a 20-tonne overhead bridge crane, and a parachute drying tower.

The facility includes a steel-framed structure enclosed with prefinished metal cladding and high-performance insulated wall assemblies. The roofing system consists of a steel deck structure with a two-ply modified bitumen membrane and insulated roof assembly. Mechanical systems include plumbing, sanitary and storm drainage, natural gas distribution, compressed air, HVAC, make-up air units, ventilation systems, heat recovery, dust collection, and building controls. Fire protection and life-safety systems include a wet-pipe sprinkler system, fire alarm system, fire department connection, emergency lighting, exit signage, and associated monitoring and control equipment. Site works include new water, sanitary, storm, electrical, communications, and site power services, including a new 300 kVA pad-mounted transformer, underground electrical distribution, communications duct banks, parking receptacles, and utility connections to support facility operations. Exterior site development also includes landscaping and paving requirements, including paved areas to support vehicle access, parking, loading, and facility operations, together with associated site restoration and landscaping. The project will meet all applicable codes and standards.

2. Documents
Technical plans and specifications are not available during this RFEOI and will be provided during the Tender Phase; however, the Standard Construction Contract Documents for Electronic Bidding, DCL 250E, are available on DCC's website: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms.
Tenderers are advised that this contract is subject to DCC's Procurement Code of Conduct, which can be downloaded at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor or supplier who has been declared ineligible or suspended by Public Services and Procurement Canada under its Ineligibility and Suspension Policy and whose period of ineligibility or suspension may not have expired will not be able to proceed to the second stage.
Bid security will be required during the Tender Phase in accordance with DCL193E- Instructions for Bidders for Electronic Bidding item 5.

3.Estimate
The Rough Order Magnitude estimate for this Contract is $12.5 Million (Current Year $).
This amount includes all construction costs, on-site work (including all required services, parking, and landscaping), site utilities, necessary redundant mechanical systems, communication conduits and wiring, backup power equipment, built-in equipment, built-in furniture, and inflation to achieve substantial completion. This amount excludes HST, design costs, travel and disbursements, consultant fees and expenses, movable equipment and furniture, IT equipment and contingencies.

4. Schedule
DCC will proceed with the Tender Phase around January 2027.
The works shall reach substantial completion no later than 420 calendar days following the notification of contract award and shall be completed no later than 35 calendar days after the substantial completion date.

5. Site visit
No site visits will be offered during the RFEOI however, during the Tender Phase, bidders will be invited to a site visit.

6. Access to information Act
Tenderers are advised that DCC is subject to the provisions of the Access to Information Act (Canada). Information submitted may be eligible for disclosure in accordance with the requirements of the Act.

7. Questions and clarifications
Any questions or requests for clarification must be submitted in writing to DCC's Coordinator, Contract Services whose contact information can be found in the Electronic Bid System.

DCC reserves the right to request clarification and/or confirmation regarding any aspect of this RFEOI to the Tenderer.

In such a case, the Coordinator, Contract Services will be responsible for making the request. The request for clarification and/or confirmation will be sent to the contact person identified on the Electronic Submission System.

8. Language of the Tender and the contract 
By submitting a response to this RFEOI, Tenderers will be invited to choose the desired official language for the tender documents and any resulting contract.
In the Tender Phase, tender documents will be published in the language chosen by the Tenderer in the Electronic Bid System.
Unless otherwise specified in the Contract, all Contract Documents to which the Contract applies or refers, as well as all deliverables, documents, reports and results of the work, services or goods that the Contractor submits, provides, or delivers to DCC or Canada in connection with the performance of the Contract, shall be in the language chosen by the Contractor on the Electronic Bid System.

9. Joint venture A joint venture is an association of two or more parties that pools their funds, assets, knowledge, expertise, or other resources into a joint business venture, sometimes called a consortium, to bid together for a requirement. Tenderers submitting interest as a joint venture will be required to clearly indicate in the Electronic Submission System that they are forming a joint venture and should provide the following information:

	the name of the joint venture, if applicable,
	the name of the representative of the joint venture, i.e., the member chosen by the other members to represent them, if applicable,
	the name of each member of the joint venture

10. Security Requirements During Construction
The Contractor will be required to hold, at all times during the performance of the construction contract, at least a valid Designated Organization Screening (DOS) issued by Public Services and Procurement Canada's (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). In the case of a joint venture, all parties to the joint venture must hold at least a valid Designated Organization Screening (DOS).

DCC has issued an Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number TRS18081_73944 to allow contractors that do not hold a valid Designated Organization Screening (DOS) security clearance to initiate the sponsorship process prior to the launch of the tender phase. For information on the sponsorship process, consult the APN on MERX or visit https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements.
To be eligible to participate in the tender phase, a Tenderer who does not hold a valid Designated Organization Verification (DOS) security clearance will be required to:

	have submitted a Sponsorship application prior to the date of publication of the Tender phase (second step Tender Phase) as indicated in the Electronic Bidding System (MERX);
	meet all material requirements of the sponsorship application package by the closing date of the tender call (Tender phase) as indicated in the Electronic Bidding System (MERX); and
	Have submitted a response to this RFEOI.

” sponsorship application” means the activity of having completed the questionnaire on the DCC web page and having forwarded the answers to the DCC Industrial Security Program (ISP)”.
” sponsorship application package” means the activity of completing and forwarding the following forms to the DCC Industrial Security Program (ISP): the Application for Registration (AFR) for Canadian legal entities form, the Company Security Officer form, the Security Agreement form, the Security Clearance form, the Fingerprints Applicant form, the Alternate Company Security form and the Personnel Screening form”.
Failure to comply with these requirements will result in a tenderer not being allowed to participate in the tender phase. However, if DCC determines, in its sole discretion that the tenderer could not comply with these requirements because of an undue administrative delay on the part of CSP or DCC, DCC may, in its sole discretion, allow the tenderer to participate in the tender phase.

11. Closing location
Responses to this RFEOI must be received through the Electronic Bidding System.  Responses sent by fax, mail or email will not be accepted.

12. Closing Date and Time
The closing date and time indicated in the Electronic Submission System will be the official closing date and time of this RFEOI.
 Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com.  Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
Advance Procurement Notice

Facilities Maintenance & Support Services
CFB Kingston, Ontario
(with Security Requirements)

1. Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice
This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals.

In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform Facility Maintenance Contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at CFB Kingston.

The purpose of this APN is to allow Facility Maintenance Contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process.
This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested Facility Maintenance Contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable).

Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB).

Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.

2. Description of the Project and Services
It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND.

APN Number:   87829
Approximate Estimate:  $40,000,000 for a period of 5 years, with 6 optional years estimated at $8M/year. Total opportunity of approximately $90M over 11 years.
Anticipated Posting: February 2027

Description:
The Facility Maintenance Services Contract will require multi-trade and single trade contractors to provide services for approximately 130 buildings of varying size and complexity across 6 sites under Real Property Operations (RP Ops) Det Kingston. The majority of the buildings are within Kingston city limits, with 1 Armoury located in Brockville, ON and 1 Armoury located in Cornwall, ON.

Description of Services:
The Contract will consist of facilities management and maintenance services that include inspection, testing, maintenance, and repairs of equipment and systems, such as HVACR, electrical, plumbing, fire detection and suppression, elevators and lifting systems, overhead cranes and vehicle hoists, backflow preventers, hydrants, security and access control, overhead doors, generators & UPS, pool systems, fume hoods, life safety systems, fuel storage tanks, roads, concrete sidewalks/curbs, fencing, as well as architectural elements such as roofs and interior repairs.

3. Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements
To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents.

notices.title: Stage 2 - Water Treatment Plant System Upgrade, Riding Mountain National Park

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
REQUIREMENT

Parks Canada requires a qualified General Contractor to complete construction-phase upgrades to the Water Treatment Plant control system at Riding Mountain National Park. The work includes upgrading the existing Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) and Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) systems, together with associated hardware, software, control panels, communications, electrical connections, operator interfaces, and field-device integration.

The Construction Contractor will supply and install the required equipment; develop or modify PLC and SCADA programming; integrate the upgraded system with existing plant processes and instrumentation; complete testing, start-up, commissioning, operator training, and closeout documentation; and correct deficiencies. All work must be coordinated with Parks Canada and plant operators to maintain safe and continuous water-treatment operations. Planned shutdowns, system cutovers, and temporary control arrangements require prior approval.

TWO STAGE SELECTION PROCESS 

This posting is the Stage Two of a two-stage solicitation process: the first stage was to evaluate the qualifications of all interested suppliers. The second stage (Stage Two) is to invite the qualified suppliers to provide further qualifications and a financial bid on the project based on the specifications and drawings.

Only qualified suppliers have been invited to bid.

Potential and interested sub-contractors are invited to add their company’s name under the section “Partner with another business”.

Maintenance and repair of manufacturing machinery, tools and equipment for CORCAN

This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, CORCAN Atlantic region.

Trade agreement:

Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: 

This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner.

Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid.

Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: 

This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers.

Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement:

This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement.

Security Requirements: This contract includes security requirements.

Nature of Requirements: 

The following is a summary of the Statement of Work for this requirement. 

The Correctional Service Canada (CSC), CORCAN in the Atlantic region, is seeking a qualified Contractor to provide professional mechanical services for the repair and maintenance of its equipment in different manufacturing sites in the provinces of New Brunswick and Nova Scotia.

Objectives: The Contractor must perform preventative maintenance and repair on tools, machinery and different equipment at various manufacturing sites in the Atlantic Region.

Deliverables: 

The Contractor’s Technical Resource must perform the work at various CSC locations in the Atlantic Region as listed below:

Community Industries Moncton – 310 Baig boulevard, Moncton, New Brunswick
Dorchester Penitentiary – 4902 Main Street, Dorchester, New Brunswick
Springhill Institution – 330 McGee Street, Springhill, Nova Scotia

1.	The Contractor must provide the Project Authority:

a.	A monthly report that includes the following as a minimum: 
i.	the date at which the Contractor performed the work; 
ii.	the Work Site where the work was completed;
iii.	a brief description of the preventative maintenance and repair services performed, including the tools, machinery, or equipment serviced, and the work completed;
iv.	The total time spent maintaining and repairing each tool, machinery, equipment.

2.	The Technical Resource (technician) must:
 
a.	Perform maintenance, repairs, installation and relocation of CORCAN tools, machinery and equipment according to the schedule of tasks to be performed. 
 
b.	Complete a time sheet and obtain approval from a CORCAN Shop Supervisor on site at the end of each workday or service call.

c.	Provide the CORCAN official on site with a service report before leaving the site. The service report must identify the tool, machinery, or equipment serviced and document the work performed, findings, test results, parts installed or recommended, any outstanding efficiencies, and the operational status of the asset. The Technical Resource must leave a copy of the service report on site and provide the original to the on-site Production Supervisor, Shop Instructor or Operations Manager upon request.

d.	Prepare and submit a schedule of planned tasks for the following week to the CORCAN Shop Supervisor each Friday.

Any conditions for participation of suppliers not specified in solicitation documentation: none.

Estimated quantity of commodity: see solicitation document statement of work and basis of payment.

Duration of Contract and Time Frame for Delivery: 

Period of the Contract: The Work is to be performed during the period of February 1, 2027, to January 31, 2028 with the option to renew for three (3) additional one-year periods.

notices.title: TBIPS SA - I.9. System Administrator and I.10. Technical Architect

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
The Office of the Secretary to the Governor General (OSGG) Information Technology Directorate is responsible for all information technology systems, including their deployment, maintenance and support. These systems include, but are not limited to, servers, desktops, applications, networks, messaging, virtualization, security, storage, authentication services, Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) and cloud computing/networking.

While the OSGG IT Directorate provides day-to-day operational support for the IT environment, certain requirements involving high-priority incidents, complex infrastructure issues, specialized technical expertise, or time-limited initiatives exceed the capacity or expertise available internally.

The OSGG requires access to a flexible source of specialized technical expertise, on an as-requested basis through Task Authorizations, to support the resolution of priority incidents, infrastructure and cloud initiatives, system optimization activities, technical planning, architecture services, documentation, and knowledge transfer requirements.

Canada may require a team of up to five (5) resources under the following TBIPS resource categories:

Two (2) I.9 System Administrator (Level 3) resources; and
Three (3) I.10 Technical Architect (Level 3) resources.

Services may involve network, infrastructure, cloud, storage, security and related technologies within the OSGG environment and will be performed through Task Authorizations issued on an as-and-when-requested basis.

notices.title: ACAN - Preventative Maintenance for Orbitrap ID-X Mass Spectrometer and Ultra-high performance liquid chromatograph (UHPLC) Instruments

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
1.	Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN)

An ACAN is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada intends to award a contract for services to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date stated in the ACAN, the Contracting Authority may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier.

2.	Definition of the requirement

The Department of Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada has a requirement for Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. to provide preventative maintenance services for one (1) Orbitrap ID-X, IC Ready Mass Spectrometer (Serial Number FSN30102) connected with Vanquish Binary Pump, Vanquish Split Sampler FT, and Vanquish Column Compartment H located at the Morden Research and Development Centre. 

The service will involve the following under an Essential Support Plan: 
-	Field Service Engineer labor, travel, and parts required for any unlimited Corrective Maintenance visits within a 72h response time.
-	Technical Support inquiries with a targeted immediate response time provided by a certified service engineer using the latest digital remote support tools. 
-	One (1) scheduled annual standard Preventive Maintenance visit including replacement parts (Standard PM Kit included).
-	Instrument Requalification (RQ) in conjunction with a scheduled Corrective Maintenance with a purchase of an add-on Operational Qualification. 
-	Access to Unity Lab Services Online Knowledge Base subscription. 
-	Software and firmware updates upon request and in conjunction with a scheduled Preventative Maintenance or Corrective Maintenance visit. 
-	10% discount on spare parts not covered by Corrective Maintenance, and accessories and consumables for the instruments, and 10% discounts off list price for any training classes purchased during the contract period. 

3.	Criteria for assessment of the Statement of Capabilities (Minimum Essential Requirements)

Any interested supplier must demonstrate by way of a statement of capabilities that it meets the following requirements: 
-	Are an authorized vendor who are certified and authorized to maintain and repair Orbitrap ID-X Mass Spectrometers and UHPLC Instruments to restore instruments operating as intended. 

4.	Applicability of the trade agreement(s) to the procurement

This procurement is subject to the following trade agreement(s):
?	Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA)
?	Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA)
?	Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement
?	Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement
?	Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement 
?	Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement
?	Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA)

5.	Justification for the Pre-Identified Supplier

Thermo Fisher Scientific owns the design of this equipment. M2	Must come equipped with a CMOS sensor, a phosphor screen, and fibre-optic coupling	
M3	Must be capable of collecting EBSD patterns with image sizes up to 1244x1024	
M4	Must have pattern acquisition speeds of up to 5700 patterns per second at 156x128 resolution	
M5	Must allow analyses at beam currents as low as 400 pA and accelerating voltages as low as 5kV	
M6	Must be capable of angular resolution up to 0.05 degrees	
M7	Must have motorized screen elevation control and insertion/retraction control	
M8	Must come equipped with a 5 diode forescatter diode (FSD) array for orientation contrast, topographic contrast, and atomic number contrast imaging	
M9	Must come with a Windows PC workstation installed with software for data acquisition and processing.	
M10 Must be capable of simultaneous EDS/EBSD mapping with an X-Max 80 model EDS detector, permitting refined phase identification using sample chemistry.
Note: The X-Max 80 is the exact model of EDS detector currently installed in the laboratory. We rely on a function where simultaneously collected EDS data is used to aid in the correct identification of crystallographically similar phases during automated EBSD analyses, and therefore any new EBSD detector must be compatible with our X-Max 80.

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE

Construction of Training Quarters Buildings 2 and 3
CFB Borden, Ontario
(with security requirements)

1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE
This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals.

In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at CFB Borden, Ontario.

The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process.

This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable).

Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.

Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB).

2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES
It is anticipated that the following 2-Step (Step 1: Request for Expression of Interest, Step 2: Tender Phase) solicitation will proceed as noted below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND.

APN Number: 88280
Approximate Estimate: $168 million for both buildings
Anticipated Posting Step 1: January 2027
Anticipated Posting Step 2: February 2027

Description:
The project comprises the construction of two new five-storey training quarters buildings at CFB Borden, Ontario. The buildings will use a site-adapted design based on the existing Training Quarters Building S-166.

The anticipated work includes building construction, mechanical and electrical systems, associated site development and connections to site services. The design will incorporate site-specific requirements and lessons learned from the existing building.

 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS
To be eligible for contract award, a tenderer or proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents.

The anticipated security screening requirement for each construction contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS).

4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship 
Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors or consultants early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors or consultants that intend to submit a tender or a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP.

Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential tenderers or proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process.

To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements.

In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors or consultants are asked to quote the following information, among other things:

	Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and
	Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN.


5. Sponsorship Process
Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors or consultants to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages.

Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor or consultant:

	Have submitted a response to the Step 1: RFEOI,
	have submitted a Sponsorship application prior to the date of publication of the Step 2: Tender Phase,
	meet all material requirements of the sponsorship application package by the closing date of the Step 2: Tender Phase, and
	Have submitted a tender to the Step 2: Tender Phase.

DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP).

Note – Contractors or Consultants that do not submit a tender will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process.

Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the tenderer or proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible.

6. Questions
Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to:

Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or
Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca

Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to:

Victor Shekofteh
Contract Coordinator
Defence Construction Canada
249-535-4651
victor.shekofteh@dcc-cdc.gc.ca


7. Disclaimer
DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the tenderer or proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the tenderer or proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.
 Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com.  Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

sections.text:
Non-Hazardous Waste Removal

This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, Grand Valley Institution, Kitchener, Ontario.

Trade agreement:	 Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), Canada Korea Trade Agreement (CKTA)

Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: 

This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner.

Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid.

Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: 
This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers.

Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: 
This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement.

Security Requirements: 
This contract does not include security requirements.

Nature of Requirements: 

The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. 

The Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) requires a contractor to provide the collection and disposal of non-hazardous waste, including recyclable and organic materials, at Grand Valley Institution. The contractor must provide all labour, materials, equipment, transportation, and bin rentals required to perform these services in accordance with applicable provincial regulations and landfill policies.

Deliverables: 

The Contractor must:

a)	Supply two (2) eight (8) cubic yard containers for Non-Hazardous Solid Waste at 1575 Homer Watson Blvd. 
b)	Supply one (1) eight (8) cubic yard container for Recyclable Cardboard at 1575 Homer Watson Blvd. 
c)	Supply ten (10) point ninety-six (96) gallon roll-out carts for Recyclable Glass and Plastic Co-Mingled at 1575 Homer Watson Blvd. 
d)	Supply six (6) thirty-two (32) gallon roll-out bins for Organic Waste at 1575 Homer Watson Blvd. 

e)	Supply one (1) four (4) cubic yard container for non-hazardous solid waste at 520 Manitou Drive. 
f)	Supply one (1) four (4) cubic yard container for cardboard at 520 Manitou Drive.
g)	Supply five (5) ninety-six (96) cubic yard roll-out carts for recyclable glass and plastic co-mingled at 520 Manitou Drive.
h)	Supply two (2) thirty-two (32) gallon roll-out bins for Organic Waste at 520 Manitou Drive.


i)	Maintain the cleanliness and appearance of bins always provided in good order.
j)	Pick-up Non-Hazardous Waste three (3) times per week (Monday, Wednesday & Friday), with the exception of Statutory Holidays. 
k)	Pick-up Cardboard Recyclables once a week, with the exception of Statutory Holidays. 
l)	Pick-up Co-Mingled Recyclables once a week, with the exception of Statutory Holidays.
m)	Pick-up Organic Waste once a week, with the exception of Statutory Holidays.
n)	Supply of all labour, materials and equipment necessary to collect, transport and properly dispose of the waste in accordance with Provincial/Federal/Municipal laws. 
o)	Provide lift weights for each stream of waste, recyclables and organics 
p)	Assume the responsibility for all waste, recyclables and organics after removal from the site.
q)	Provide weight verification slips from the landfill site, if requested, to support invoiced amounts. 


Any conditions for participation of suppliers not specified in solicitation documentation: none.

Estimated quantity of commodity: see solicitation document statement of work and basis of payment.

Duration of Contract and Time Frame for Delivery: 

Period of the Contract: The Work is to be performed during the period of January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2030.

Telephone number: 613-650-1203
E-mail: robin.riha@csc-scc.gc.ca

notices.title: Develop Wayfinding Strategy for Mississippi Lake National Wildlife Area (MLNWA), St Clair National Wildlife Area (SCNWA) and Big Creek National Wildlife Area (BCNWA)

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
Background
Canadian Wildlife Service (CWS) Ontario manages 10 National Wildlife Areas in Ontario.  Two of these, Prince Edward Point National Wildlife Area (PEPNWA) and Big Creek National Wildlife Area (BCNWA) have also been designated as Connecting Canadians to Nature sites.  Out of more than 60 National Wildlife Areas across the country only 10 have been designated as Connecting Canadians to Nature sites. These 10 sites as well as select few of the other NWAs are open to the public and provide opportunities for people to experience and connect with nature. 
CWS Ontario is working to improve accessibility and enhance visitors’ experiences at publicly accessible NWAs in Ontario.  In 2025, a wayfinding strategy and upgrades to signage were completed at PEPNWA to improve accessibility for visitors.  CWS Ontario is now looking to implement similar improvements at other publicly accessible NWAs in the province using guidance developed for PEPNWA.

Objective
Develop Wayfinding Strategy for Mississippi Lake National Wildlife Area (MLNWA), St Clair National Wildlife Area (SCNWA) and Big Creek National Wildlife Area (BCNWA) and complete signage designs as required based on outcomes of individual site visits and using guidance outlined in Design Brief (Appendix B) and Wayfinding Signage Design Intent (Appendix C) previously prepared for PEPNWA.

Primary Care Physician Services for the Beaver Creek Institution - Medium Security (Stream A) and Beaver Creek Institution - Minimum Security (Stream B)

This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, Ontario Region.

Trade agreement:	 This procurement is not subject to any trade agreement.

Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers.

Competitive Procurement Strategy: compliant bid with the highest technical score.

Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers.

Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement.

Security Requirements: This contract includes security requirements.

Nature of Requirements:  The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. 

The Correctional Service of Canada has a requirement to provide Primary Care Physician services for the Beaver Creek Institution – Medium Security and Beaver Creek Institution – Minimum Security in the Ontario Region.

Objectives: The Contractor (Primary Care Physician) must provide integrated patient centred medical services to  patients in collaboration with the Institution's inter-disciplinary health care team that includes, but is not limited to: nurses (nurse practitioners, registered nurses, registered psychiatric nurses, licensed practical nurses, registered practical nurses), primary care physicians, social workers, dentists, denturists, infectious disease physician specialist, pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, psychologists, psychiatrists, behavioural science technicians, mental health providers, psychoeducators, personal support workers, client care attendants, optometrist, physiotherapists, x-ray technologists, foot care specialists, occupational therapists, administrative personnel and other healthcare professionals.

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE

Standing Offer for Energy Performance Contract Procurement and Financial Advisory Services
(with security requirements)

1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE
This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals.

In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform consultants of an upcoming Standing Offer opportunity.

The purpose of this APN is to allow consultants to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process.

This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential Standing Offer, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested consultants to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances.

Please note that there is no guarantee that this Standing Offer will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.

2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES
It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted below. This is conditional upon funding approval by DND.

APN Number: EPFS2601
Approximate Estimate: 800,000$
Anticipated Posting: January 2027

Description: Energy Performance Contract Procurement and Financial Advisory Services

The Consultant will be required to provide “as and when required” procurement and financial advisory services in support of Energy Performance Contracts (EPCs).
The services may include, but are not limited to, the following:

	Review and provide procurement and financial advice on the contractual documents including the Request for Proposal (RFP) financial evaluation criteria;
	Support DCC in preparing draft responses to financial questions from Proponents during the procurement phase;
	Review and provide advice on the financial evaluation framework to assess the Proponent’s financial capabilities;
	Assist DCC with the evaluation of the financial component of the Proponents proposals;
	Support DCC in the review and analysis of the financial proposal received following the feasibility study;
	Assist in the negotiation and finalizing the final terms of the contract.

The objective is to select one (1) consultant capable of providing deliverables in both official languages (English and French).
The estimated value of the Standing Offer is approximately $500,000 over an initial two (2)-year period, with the option to extend the Standing Offer for up to two (2) additional one (1)-year periods and to increase its value by an additional $300,000 at any time. The total estimated potential value of the Standing Offer is approximately $800,000 over four (4) years.

3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS
To be eligible for the issuance of a Standing Offer, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents.

The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS).

4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship 
Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing consultants early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, consultants that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP.

Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process.

To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements.

In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants are asked to quote the following information, among other things:

	Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and
	Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN.

5. Sponsorship Process
Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages.

Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant:

	has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX,
	has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and
	has submitted a proposal,  

DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP).

Note – Consultants that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process.

Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible.

6. Questions
Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to:

Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or
Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca

Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to:

Patricia Biernat
Procurement Specialist
Defence Construction Canada
819-500-8074
Patricia.Biernat@dcc-cdc.gc.ca

7. Disclaimer
DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.

notices.buyer: Defence Construction Canada - National Capital Region

sections.label: 사업 내용
sections.text:
ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE

Construction Management Services, Whitehorse cadet training centre 
whitehorse, yukon 
(with security requirements)

1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE
This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals.

In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at Whitehorse, Yukon.

The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process.

This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable).

Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.

Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB).

2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES

The objective of this contract is to recapitalize both vertical and horizontal infrastructure at the Whitehorse Cadet Training Centre (WCTC) through a multi-year program.

The existing WCTC site includes a diverse portfolio of facilities comprising 39 buildings with a total floor area of approximately 5,000 m². These facilities include barracks with associated ablution areas, classrooms, a combined kitchen/dining/administration building, a large storage warehouse, and various workshops and auxiliary support structures.

The recapitalization program will encompass the renovation of existing buildings, as well as the demolition and reconstruction of selected facilities, to modernize and enhance the overall functionality of the site.

Project delivery will be undertaken using a Construction Management (CM) contract.

The Government of Canada is committed to advancing reconciliation and fostering meaningful engagement with Indigenous Peoples. In support of these commitments, DND aims to create opportunities for Indigenous businesses and communities through meaningful subcontracting, employment, and training related to the proposed project.

To align with these objectives, the successful proponents will be required to develop an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP) as part of the CM contract. The IBPs will outline proposed initiatives and opportunities for Indigenous participation, including subcontracting, employment, and training activities.

It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND.

APN: APN_NPYKCM01
Approximate Estimate: $50M
Anticipated Posting: Winter 2027

3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS
To be eligible for contract award, a proponent  will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents.

The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS)

4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship 
Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors  that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP.

Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process.

To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements.

In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things:

	Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and
	Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN.


5. Sponsorship Process
Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages.

Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor

	has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX,
	has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and
	has submitted a proposal.  

DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP).

Note – Contractors  that do not submit a proposal  will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process.

Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible.

6. Questions
Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to:

Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or
Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca

Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to:



Eric Ndayambaza
Coordinator, Contract Services
Defence Construction Canada
Eric.Ndayambaza@dcc-cdc.gc.ca
Email: +(1) 343-576-9347




7. Disclaimer
DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.

Challenge title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) decision-making process visibility, traceability and compliance governance
Challenge sponsor: Shared Services Canada (SSC) 

Funding Mechanism: Contract
MAXIMUM CONTRACT VALUE:
Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge.

Phase 2: 
• The maximum funding available for any Phase 2 contract resulting from this Challenge is : $2,000,000.00 CAD excluding applicable taxes, shipping, travel and living expenses, as required.
• The maximum duration for any Phase 2 contracts resulting from this Challenge is up to 20 months (excluding submission of the final report).
• Estimated number of Phase 2 contracts: 1

This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to award any contract for the total approximate funding. Final decisions on the number of Phase 1 and Phase 2 (amend as applicable) awards will be made by Canada on the basis of factors such as evaluation results, departmental priorities and availability of funds. Canada reserves the right to make partial awards and to negotiate project scope changes.
Note: Selected companies are eligible to receive one contract per phase per challenge.

Travel: No travel required. 
Kick-off Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference.
Progress Review Meeting(s): Any progress review meetings will be conducted by telephone or videoconference.
Final Review Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference.

Problem Statement:

Challenge Statement Summary
The Government of Canada (GoC) is committed to the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) compliant with its AI Strategy and Guiding Principles, see references noted in this challenge notice.
The widespread adoption of AI technologies has created opportunities to enhance decision-making and improve service delivery within the GoC. In fostering the responsible usage of AI, the GoC has established an adoption strategy and guiding principles. To support adherence and implementation, the GoC is interested in testing solutions that provide visibility into AI decision-making processes, enhance the traceability of AI outputs, and ensure that AI models comply with Canadian laws and international standards and best practices.
Despite the availability of AI governance solutions from Canadian companies and international providers, existing offerings typically require significant manual effort. This effort is particularly evident in interpreting evolving AI governance requirements, applying them to specific AI systems, updating controls and assessments, and identifying their ecosystem-wide impacts. 
The challenge seeks innovation to advance capabilities for identifying and incorporating evolving governance requirements, determining their potential impact on registered AI systems, associated controls, assessments, and evidence, and supporting timely reassessment, all while maintaining explainability, traceability, auditability, and human oversight.

Details:

Essential (mandatory) Outcomes
The proposed solution must:

1.	Support the continuous alignment of registered AI systems with relevant Canadian regulations, policies, directives, and other governance requirements and  be able to identify potentially affected systems and indicate when a reassessment is required.

2.	Demonstrate interoperability with enterprise systems, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) platforms and governance solutions and the solution can be integrated with minimal customization.
2A. Demonstrate the ability to exchange governance information with enterprise systems and AI/ML lifecycle tools through standards-based Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), connectors and interoperable data exchange mechanisms. Governance information may include AI system metadata, risk assessments, compliance findings, audit evidence, monitoring results, approvals and decision records. As an example: This governance information includes but is not limited to, information about the AI system, ownership, intent, deployment status, funding state, client information, system objectives, assessments, algorithmic impact assessment, control requirements (playbooks).
2B. Demonstrate how governance information can be collected, aggregated and maintained across multiple systems through APIs, connectors and data exchange mechanisms.
2C. Leverage open standards and documented interfaces to reduce dependency on proprietary technologies enabling interoperability across diverse enterprise environments.

3.	Demonstrate how administrative, support and access to governance information and data can be restricted, monitored and controlled in accordance with the GoC requirements.
3A. Enable organizations to define and manage data residency requirements, retention, access and deletion of policies and information without vendor intervention.

4.	Enable assessment and reassessment of registered AI systems applicable AI governance requirements, policies, standards, directives while supporting reassessment when governance requirements, assessment frameworks are added modified, replaced or retired. The solution must demonstrate the ability to translate AI governance requirements into traceable controls assess whether applicable controls have been satisfied and identify non-conformities.
4A. Enable authorized users to add, modify, version, replace or retire governance requirements and assessment frameworks to individual AI systems or groups. Demonstrate compliance assessment at minimum against the Policy on Service and Digital,  Directive on Automated Decision-Making, Algorithmic Impact Assessment, AI Strategy and AI ethics and responsibilities. 
4B. Demonstrate the ability to add, modify, version, replace and retire governance requirements, controls and assessment criteria, and assign them to individual AI systems or groups of AI systems. while supporting the application of different assessment criteria to different AI systems based on their intended use, risk profile or governance requirements Offerors are encouraged to prove extensibility to additional internationally recognized governance frameworks and standards, including the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the EU Act.
4C. Generate human-readable explanations of assessment and reassessment results. Each finding must identify the applicable requirement, evidence considered, assessment result and confidence score or a certainty measure. user.
4D. Collect, link, and retain assurance artefacts including control mapping, assessment records, evidence references, approvals, exceptions, attestations, remediation actions and audit histories. The system must identify whether each artifact was provided by an authorised individual [Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)].
4E. Provide measurable results and clearly distinguish between results when performing a compliance assessments to determine whether compliance is met, partially met, not met, not applicable and unable to determine.

5.	Allow for authorised reviewers to validate reject, modify or annotate findings and retain and audit log history for decisions.

6.	Support the assessment and reassessment of risks associated with data, models and AI-generated outputs and incorporate the resulting information into governance assessments and assurance activities.
6A. Support assessment of data related risks and quality measures relevant to the registered AI system including the establishment of baseline measures and thresholds to maintain a traceable record of issues. 
6B. Enable organizations to define, evaluate and reassess risk, performance and quality measures appropriate to a registered AI system. including configurable measures, thresholds, and evaluation criteria to maintain a traceable record of assessment outcomes.
6C. Support the evaluation and monitoring of AI-generated outputs against criteria appropriate to the system’s intended use and identified risks including accuracy, quality, fairness, consistency, safety, and alignment with defined operational requirements. 


Additional Outcomes
The proposed solution should:

1.  Support deployment in on-premises, private cloud, and Canadian-hosted cloud environments without requiring significant architectural modification.

2. 	Provide bilingual functionality, including user interfaces, documentation, reporting, and governance workflows, in both English an French.                                                                                                                                                   

3. 	Support multiple organizations, departments, or domains within a shared platform while enabling independent governance policies, controls, reporting, and oversight for each tenant.

4. Generate governance reports, alerts, and notifications and integrate with enterprise collaboration, communication, and ticketing/case management systems.

Background and context
As Shared Services Canada (SSC) expands the use of AI solutions, including generative and Agentic AI, there is a growing need for a consistent, centralized, and scalable approach to AI governance. Current governance activities may rely on separate processes, manual tracking, and fragmented documentation, which can limit real-time visibility into AI system inventories, risk posture, compliance status, policy alignment, and decision-making evidence.
